title: Residential Electricity Supply Plan Changes: Peak-Cycle Reduction
content:
**Rule.** On a Residential Electricity Supply plan change, the largest kWh on any single on-peak or all-hours energy line of the agreement is taken; at 900 kWh or more the high peak-cycle reduction of 0.15 cents per kWh applies, from 600 up to but not including 900 kWh the mid peak-cycle reduction of 0.08 cents per kWh applies, and below 600 kWh none applies.

| Largest single on-peak or all-hours line | Peak-cycle reduction (cents per kWh) |
|---|---|
| 900 kWh or more | 0.15 |
| 600 up to but not including 900 kWh | 0.08 |
| below 600 kWh | none |

**Lines read.** Every on-peak and every all-hours energy line on the agreement, whenever billed; off-peak lines are not read. The single highest kWh among them decides the tier.

**Boundaries.** A largest line of exactly 900 kWh takes 0.15 cents and one of 899 kWh takes 0.08 cents; exactly 600 kWh takes 0.08 cents and 599 kWh takes none.

**Example (hypothetical).** An agreement whose largest all-hours line is 1,140 kWh in a January cycle takes 0.15 cents, however low its other cycles were.
